- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., 65+ to 68+), then corrects — apply lagged correction: if forecast > true by >5%, reduce next period’s forecast by 2–3%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 65, and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 1–2% per period.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates when sentiment is high and price is trending up — increase forecast by 1–2% if sentiment > 0.7 and price > 65.
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is below 60, model often fails to recover — increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment < 0.3 and price < 60.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps to 1.00 but price is flat, don’t increase forecast unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
